svg.aria-label: nes-bench bridge v1c: v1b as a printed shield, the hands on board (sheet 1 of 5: the console side)

g.text: nes-bench bridge v1c: v1b as a printed shield, the hands on board (sheet 1 of 5: the console side)
the circuit that passed bench-check on 2026-10-17, net for net, on an UNO shield; keyed cables, the reset opto and the power relay as bare parts. 2026-10-17. Not built.

svg.text: THE CONSOLE PORT, THE INVERTER AND THE REGISTER, ALL AT +5V (AS v1b)
THE CLOCK PIN'S FILTER, ON THE BOARD
MEASURED 2026-09-09: supply on 5, 6 and 7 not carried; pin 5 not used here
five spare inputs tied to GND
one 100nF across each of U1, U2 and U3,
at the chip's own supply pins
v1b's filter (MEASURED 2026-09-15: D0's own edge re-clocked the 165). The UNO's
D2 still counts CON_CLK ahead of R2, exactly as on the breadboard. On 2026-10-16
R2 sat one breadboard row off the clock lead, the walk read bit 0 in all eight
slots, and only a probe on U2 pin 2 could have shown it: TP4 (sheet 3) is that probe.
